title: bug: the guest supervisor's relay leaves a finished job's background processes running and stops watching host EOF once the job closes its output pipes
description: run_bridge stands the guard down on a normal finish without killpg (run_install always kills), so `sleep 300 &` or a setsid child outlives the job until VM deletion, contrary to check-evidence's teardown 'killed-and-reaped'; and pump stops polling in_fd once both output pipes close, so a host EOF (header: exit 74) goes unnoticed while the job runs on. Also: a bridge request pending at job exit turns a real observation into SESSION_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (guest-session.mjs:169; runAgentJob has no caller yet), and the header's exit 75, materialize's "leaves neither" comment and snapshot-import.mjs's "limit codes surface unchanged" disagree with the code. Changes supervisorSha256, so certification reports must be re-run.
definitionOfDone: After any job ends, no process of its group or session survives the observation frame, and a host EOF is acted on while a job with closed output pipes still runs, with tests.
The supervisor header and the cited comments match the code.

implementationPlan.description: Use test-driven-development in local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Replace S11's explicitly obsolete requirement that a grandchild survive normal completion with a death-before-observation assertion; this is an intentional behavior correction, not assertion weakening. Cover exit0, nonzero and signalled jobs with a lingering child that keeps output open or redirects it closed. Reuse existing guarded/session/frame helpers, accumulating PID output safely across chunks; assert the actual original exit/signal, one final observation only after owned descendants are gone, bounded completion, and an unrelated sentinel started by the test remains alive. Add a real-Python case whose job closes both output pipes but keeps running: close host in_fd after a deterministic ready/closed-output handshake, expect74 promptly with no observation and owned job cleanup. Add the same quiet-output case with malformed host data expecting76 and keep catchable-signal75 coverage. Existing task-a4a729ddaa8942679e8ae7cd57bd42f1 kernel-boundary tests cover setsid/setpgid/double-fork escape and supervisor SIGKILL; retain those unchanged and exercise its real root-Linux path when validating the completion boundary. Test cleanup may signal only exact recorded PIDs this test started, never names/UIDs/session scans; isolate privileged probes in owned namespaces.
implementationPlan.note:
RED tests in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs, written before the supervisor change.

**New and changed rows**
- GLOBAL_PIDS: gpid/gfork read procfs on Linux and fall back to os.getpid/os.fork elsewhere. It is ported from the a46b60e6 prototype, without gsid (unused here), so the new rows already report global pids under a root runner.
- S11 (the old survival row is reversed): it now runs 6 tests, exit 0/7/SIGTERM × a lingering child that holds or has closed the output pipes. Each asserts:
  - the job's own observation is kept, through session();
  - the pids come from the concatenated stdout outputs (reportedPids);
  - an OBSERVE harness hooks m.write_frame and checks at the observation write that every reported pid is reaped, a zombie, or has SIGKILL pending in /proc ShdPnd (Linux);
  - relay() returns in under 10 s;
  - a Node-spawned detached sentinel stays running;
  - the descendants are not running within 5 s.
  Cleanup kills only recorded pids and the sentinel ChildProcess.
- S17: since pump will keep polling the listener, the test SIGSTOPs its own supervisor (by recorded pid) before connecting, then sends SIGTERM and SIGCONT. The connection stays queued, so the row keeps its subject. The assertion is unchanged.
- S18 ×3: the job writes its pid, closes both output pipes, then does a FIFO rendezvous as the closed-output handshake and settles 0.5 s. Then host EOF must give 74, a malformed frame 76, and SIGTERM 75, each:
  - promptly (under 5 s after the act);
  - with frames hello+output only;
  - with the job dead within 5 s.
- S19: GUARD is patched to write '++'. The stray start byte must fail closed: 74, frames [hello].

**RED on the unchanged supervisor** (Node 24.21.0, env -i, in place, scripts/tests harness only)
- tests 11, pass 2 (S17, S18-SIGTERM), fail 9:
  - S11 'open' ×3: ETIMEDOUT at 20 s; pump waits on the child's pipes.
  - S11 'closed' ×3: dead=[true,false]; the child can still run at the observation.
  - S18 eof/malformed: ETIMEDOUT; host input is not watched after the output closes.
  - S19: 75 after the 60 s harness timeout, not 74.
- No marked process (MOE_97341_MARK=red1) was left alive.

implementationPlan.description: Make guard completion, not stdout/stderr lifetime, drive relay. After startup read returns '+', send the existing life-pipe stand-down byte immediately (as run_install already does); catch BrokenPipeError as the existing self-killed-group case. Extend pump to watch start_end in the SAME Bridge selector alongside host stdin, termination wakeup, agent sockets and output pipes. Keep servicing host EOF/protocol/signals even after both output streams close; no subsequent blocking completion-only read that stops watching host. An EOF on start_end marks guard completion; any unexpected control byte fails closed. Before reaping, SIGKILL the owned original process group while the unreaped guard pins its id (ProcessLookupError is benign), then drain remaining output to EOF. Only when completion EOF and both output EOFs are established may reap supply the single observation. Preserve raw wait status: cleanup must never turn a job's0/7/signal into a different observed result. The prerequisite's root-Linux kernel boundary guarantees all escaped descendants already ended before completion EOF; do not replace it with process scans or broaden kill scope. Keep finally teardown on all errors, close fds/selector/socket exactly once, retain signal-handler/wakeup restoration, and keep error handling mapping71 startup,74 I/O/hostEOF,75 caught signal,76 protocol. No busy polling, extra thread, second selector loop or public frame change.
implementationPlan.note:
Changes in guest-supervisor.py:

**run_bridge**
- The stand-down byte is written right after the startup '+', as run_install does. BrokenPipeError is still the self-killed-group case.
- pump(child, out_fd, bridge, start_end, wait) registers start_end in the same Bridge selector as the host in_fd, the wakeup pipe, the agent socket, the connections and both output pipes. It loops until start_end and both outputs are at EOF, so host EOF (74), protocol errors (76) and signals (75) stay serviced after the output closes.
- On start_end EOF (the guard has exited, unreaped), pump calls os.killpg(child.pid, SIGKILL) with `except GROUP_GONE`, then drains the outputs to EOF.
- Any byte on start_end after '+' raises OSError, which fails closed with 74 and the finally kills the group.
- reap supplies the single observation only after pump returns. The trailing termination.read(start_end) is gone.
- The guard is a zombie when the group is killed, so the raw wait status is unchanged.

**GROUP_GONE**
- Added verbatim after pump(), as in a4c8204d (fix/ci-pr230).
- The finally block and run_install now use `except GROUP_GONE:`, identical to a4c8204d.
- pump's last two lines are unchanged, so a merge of that branch sees identical hunks.
- `grep -c "except ProcessLookupError"` prints 0.

**Unchanged**: no new thread, selector, poll or frame. Teardown and handler/wakeup restoration are as before. GUARD's code is untouched.

**Verification** (Node 24.21.0, env -i, scripts/tests harnesses run in place)
- S rows: 28/28 pass, about 9 s.
- bridge + guard + check: 150 tests, 148 pass, 0 fail, 2 pre-existing skips (LA5, K9). That includes G1–G9, the real root PID-namespace path through unprivileged userns.
- `unshare -r` run of S11 ×6, S18 ×3 and S19: 10/10 pass.
- No marked leftover processes.

Orderings reviewed against the code:
(a) Output EOF, then start EOF: pump keeps waiting on start, host and wake. At start EOF it runs killpg; GROUP_GONE covers a zombie-only group. Then the loop ends, reap, observation.
(b) Start EOF first, with lingering holders: killpg while the unreaped guard pins the pgid, drain to EOF (buffered output kept), then the observation. As root the namespace is already empty, because the guard exits only after waitpid(init).
(c) Host EOF, a malformed frame or a signal while the outputs are closed: 74, 76 or 75 through the same selector. The finally kills and reaps the group. No observation.
(d) A signal after pump returns: no further wait() call, so the true observation is written and relay() returns 0 (the job had completed).
(e) The job SIGKILLs its own group: a stand-down EPIPE is ignored and the observation is SIGKILL (S13).
(f) A stray start byte: 74, fail closed.
(g) Queued agent connections: Bridge.close accepts, then closes them, so peers read EOF, never a reset (S17). Requests are now served while a quiet job runs; before, they stalled after output EOF.
(h) A late host frame after pump: never read. The host side's abandonment of pending requests is 5ee846b6's contract (H9 passes).

- No observation before the group kill. killpg only targets child.pid, and only while it is unreaped; no kill happens after reap.
- 71/74/75/76 are unchanged in meaning. The only change: the stray byte is 74, and host EOF in the quiet window now gives 74 where it used to be ignored. comments.author: architect-66fd8127
comments.content:
Heads-up from task-a46b60e6, which depends on this row. It is informational only and does not change your plan or DoD.

Under a root runner (`unshare -r`, or real root in a guest), GUARD unshares a PID namespace. Inside the job, os.getpid() and os.getppid() return namespace-local numbers (2 and 1), and so does a fork() return value. A job that calls kill() on the harness's outer pid gets ESRCH. The guest's procfs still reports global pids.

a46b converts the existing rows after you land: S6, AGENT_CHILD, GROUP_JOB, S11, S12, S15, S16, S17, J4, K3, KI1 and KI2. It uses readlink('/proc/self'), /proc/<pid>/stat fields, a fork whose child pipes its global pid to the parent, and harness-side signals. If your NEW rows send job pids to the host (your S11 rewrite, the quiet-output host-EOF case), you may already read them from procfs. Either way, a46b audits and converts whatever remains. Please don't change other rows for this.

Reference: Serena memory task-task-a46b60e6aa63422fbd63934d17238396-prototype.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
Governor plan amendment for step 2 (from architect-b58e1112, msg-db71184c). It is binding for whoever works this row.

Step 2 says "SIGKILL the owned original process group while the unreaped guard pins its id (ProcessLookupError is benign)". Do NOT write a bare `except ProcessLookupError` at that killpg. Catch GROUP_GONE instead.

Why: when the job leaves nothing behind (the usual case), the group holds only the zombie guard. Linux treats the killpg as a no-op, but darwin raises PermissionError. The completion would then fail on macOS, and the macOS CI leg runs the bridge tests. Your WSL gate and QA would not see this.

How:
- If scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py already defines GROUP_GONE (the CI fix for PR #230, branch fix/ci-pr230, is due to land on this branch soon), reuse it: `except GROUP_GONE:`.
- If it does not exist yet, add this exact definition after pump(), with its comment, so the later merge sees an identical line on both sides:
```
# killpg errors that mean no member of the job group is left to kill: ESRCH, and on darwin, where only the tests run this
# file, EPERM for a group of zombies (Linux signals one as a no-op).
GROUP_GONE = (ProcessLookupError, PermissionError) if sys.platform == 'darwin' else ProcessLookupError
```
Check: after your change, `grep -c "except ProcessLookupError" scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py` must print 0.

completionSummary:

- After '+', the guard gets the stand-down byte at once.
- pump watches the guard's start pipe in the Bridge's one selector (host, agent socket and wakeup fd included) until start EOF and both output EOFs.
